ITQAN:v2p364/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p364/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p364/r6.claim: فتيلا is the thread in the groove of a date stone; al-Nabigha cites the word in a line about nothing being taken from enemies.
ITQAN:v2p364/r6.anchor: قال التي تكون في شق النواة أما سمعت قول النابغة

DAMGHANI:v1p218/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r3.claim: Yuzakkī can mean to vindicate or acquit someone.
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r3.anchor: أي ولا يبرئهم مثلها في سورة الكهف

SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r1.claim: ألم تر has already been discussed in the same way elsewhere.
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: { ألم تر }: تقدم مثله

SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r2.claim: بل turns away from their claim to purify themselves.
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r2.anchor: و " بل " إضراب عن تزكيتهم أنفسهم.

SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa supplies an omitted clause before the correction: ‘They erred; rather, God purifies whom He wills.’
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r3.anchor: قبل هذا الإضراب جملة قال: " تقديره: أخطؤوا بل الله يزكي من يشاء

SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r4.claim: ولا يظلمون may be circumstantial from what precedes or an independent sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r4.anchor: يجوز أن يكون حالا مما تقدم، وأن يكون مستأنفا،

SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r5.claim: The pronoun most likely refers to من يشاء: those God purifies lose none of their purification; من is nearest, and بل begins a disconnected correction.
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r5.anchor: والأول أظهر؛ لأن " من " أقرب مذكور، ولأن " بل " إضراب منقطع ما بعدها عما قبلها.

SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r6.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r6.claim: The pronoun may instead refer to those who purify themselves, or to both groups.
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r6.anchor: وأن يعود على الذين يزكون، وأن يعود على القبيلين

SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r7.claim: For the two-group interpretation, self-purifiers lose none of their punishment and those purified by God lose none of their reward.
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r7.anchor: فذاك لا ينقص من عقابه شيئا، وهذا لا ينقص من ثوابه شيئا.

SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats the clause as independent with the pronoun referring to both groups; the author says this antecedent is also possible with a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r8.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " ويجوز أن يكون مستأنفا أي: من زكى نفسه، ومن زكاه الله " انتهى

SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r9.claim: فتيلا is a second object because the first object has become نائب الفاعل; alternatively it is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, as in the prior discussion of مثقال ذرة.
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r9.anchor: { فتيلا } مفعول ثان، لأن الأول قام مقام الفاعل، ويجوز أن يكون نعت مصدر محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r10.claim: فتيل is the fine thread in a date stone’s groove, a proverbial measure of trivial smallness; it may also be lint rubbed from the fingers, with فعيل meaning مفعول.
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r10.anchor: والفتيل: خيط رقيق في شق النواة، يضرب به المثل في القلة، وقيل: هو ما خرج من بين إصبعيك

SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r11.claim: Arab usage groups four tiny things around a date stone: فتيل, نقير, قطمير, and ثفروق; the first three occur in scripture.
SAMIN-DURR:4:49/r11.anchor: وقد ضربت العرب المثل في القلة التافهة بأربعة أشياء اجتمعن في النواة، وهي: الفتيل والنقير وهو النقرة التي في ظهر النواة

ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r1.claim: Some gloss alam tara as, Have you not been informed?
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r1.anchor: (ألم تر): ألم تخبر في قول بعضهم.

ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r2.claim: Language scholars explain alam tara as, Do you not know? Its interrogative wording conveys information: know their story, or has your knowledge reached them?
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r2.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة ألم تعلم وتأويله سؤال فيه معنى الإعلام. تأويله أعلم قصتهم، وعلى مجرى اللغة ألم ينته علمك إلى هؤلاء

ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r3.claim: The Jews claim that they are pure; zakāʾ linguistically means a thing's growth in goodness.
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r3.anchor: ومعنى يزكون انفسهم أي تزعمون أنهم أزكياء. وتأويل قولنا: زكاء الشيء: في اللغة نماؤه في الصلاح.

ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r4.claim: A report says Jews brought their children and asked Muhammad if they had sins; after he said no, they claimed they too were sinless, saying their deeds were forgiven by night and day.
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r4.anchor: وكانوا جاؤوا إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بأطفالهم فقالوا: يا محمد أعلى هؤلاء ذنوب؟ فقال النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لا، فقالوا كذا نحن، ما نعمل بالليل يغفر بالليل، وما نعمل بالنهار يغفر بالنهار.

ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r5.claim: God purifies whomever He wills, that is, He makes that person pure.

ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r6.claim: One explanation of fatīl is the dirt or fuzz rolled between one's fingers.
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم: الفتيل ما تفتله بين إصبعيك من الوسخ

ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r7.claim: Another explanation of fatīl is the fiber or husk inside a date stone.
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم: الفتيل ما كان في باطن النواة من لحائها.

ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r8.claim: Exegetes also identify fatīl as the thread on the back of a date stone from which the palm sprouts; qitmīr is its whole surrounding husk.
ZAJJAJ:v2p60/r8.anchor: وقالوا في التفسير: ماكان في ظهرها وهو الذي تنبت منه النخلة. والقطمير جملة ما التف عليها من لحائها.

ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r1.claim: The people who deem themselves pure are Jews claiming chosen status and Christians who rely on Jesus' vicarious atonement for humanity's sins.
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r1.anchor: the Jews, who consider, themselves to be "God's chosen people" and, therefore, a priori destined for God's grace, and the Christians, who believe in Jesus' "vicarious atonement" for the sins of mankind.

ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r2.claim: Although Christians profess one God, elevating Jesus to divine manifestation and worshipping saints assigns divine or semi-divine status to humans and constitutes deeper shirk.
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r2.anchor: the Christians by their elevation of Jesus to the status of a manifestation of God in human form and their open worship of a hierarchy of saints

ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r3.claim: Jews' attribution of overriding lawmaking authority to Talmudic scholars is also shirk; Asad compares this to 9:31.
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r3.anchor: the Jews by their attribution of law-giving powers to the great Talmudic scholars, whose legal verdicts are supposed to override, if need be, any ordinance of the scriptures (cf. in this respect 9: 31).

ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r4.claim: The condemnation also applies to Muslims who worship saints or give them reverence due to God alone.
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r4.anchor: It goes without saying that this condemnation applies also to those Muslims who have fallen into the sin of worshipping saints and according them something of the reverence which is due to God alone.

ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r5.claim: In context, the phrase covers people who claim belief in one God yet commit shirk in its deeper sense; this connects the warning to the preceding verse's shirk.
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n66/r5.anchor: the expression "those who consider themselves pure" comprises, in this context, all who think of themselves as believing in the One God (simply because they do not consciously worship a plurality of deities) but are, nevertheless, guilty of the sin of shirk in the deeper sense of this term.

ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n67/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n67/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n67/r1.claim: Fatil is a slender thread rolled between the fingers, also used for the tiny fiber in a date stone's cleft; idiomatically it means a hair's breadth.
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n67/r1.anchor: a 'fatil' is any "slender thread which one rolls between one's fingers" - a term which is also, but by no means exclusively, applied to the tiny fibre adhering to the cleft of the date-stone

ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n67/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n67/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n67/r2.claim: Purity is not a group's privilege and is possible only through God's grace, since humanity is weak; Asad also points to 53:32.
ASAD-NOTES:4:49#n67/r2.anchor: the above passage implies, firstly, that spiritual purity is not the privilege of any particular group or community, and, secondly, that one can become or remain pure only by God's grace, for "man has been created weak" (verse 28 above). See also note on the second paragraph of 53:32.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p116/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p116/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p116/r2.claim: “Fatīlan” can denote the physical thread in a date stone or function as an absolute object meaning no amount of injustice, however small; both senses are intended.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p116/r2.anchor: الفتيل هو الخيط في شق النواة فهل المقصود شيئاً ماديا (مفعول به) أو شيئاً من الظلم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r5.claim: Using the parallel quoted as ولا تظلمون فتيلا, he explains that فتيل can mean the physical thread in a date stone or a tiny amount of injustice, and the wording conveys both senses.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p565/r5.anchor: الفتيل هو الخيط في شق النواة فهل المقصود شيئاً ماديا (مفعول به)

IBNMUJAHID:v1p234/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p234/r8.speaker: نافع، أبو عمرو، عاصم، ابن عامر؛ القراء في 4:49
IBNMUJAHID:v1p234/r8.claim: These readers use tāʾ in 4:77; all agree on yāʾ in يظلمون at 4:49.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p234/r8.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر ﴿ تظلمون ﴾ بالتاء ولم يختلفوا في قوله ﴿ يزكي من يشاء ولا يظلمون فتيلا ﴾ النساء 49

NASHR:v2p249/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p249/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p249/r7.claim: For the repeated phrase, Ibn Kathīr, Abū Jaʿfar, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read in the third person; Rawḥ has both a third-person route and second person from his other transmitters.
NASHR:v2p249/r7.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو جعفر وحمزة والكسائي، وخلف بالغيب

NASHR:v2p249/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p249/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p249/r8.claim: Readers unanimously use third person in بل الله يزكي من يشاء ولا يظلمون فتيلا; the third-person من يشاء governs the following clause.
NASHR:v2p249/r8.anchor: على الغيب في قوله تعالى: من هذه السورة بل الله يزكي من يشاء ولا يظلمون فتيلا

NASHR:v2p249/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p249/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p249/r9.claim: The author explains that the following verb has no second-person variant because من يشاء itself is third person.
NASHR:v2p249/r9.anchor: لأجل أن قوله من يشاء للغيب فرد عليه

QIRAAT-ER:4:49:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:49:15#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:4:49:15#1/r1.claim: A liaison variant gives the next verse's initial hamza ḍamma instead of the usual linking kasra, without changing fatīlan's meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:4:49:15#1/r1.anchor: affects liaison between this ayah's final word and the next ayah's opening imperative

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p164/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p164/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p164/r1.claim: Al-Hasan identifies those who claim to purify themselves as Jews and Christians, who say they are God’s children and beloved and that only their communities enter Paradise.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p164/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم ﴾ قال هم اليهود والنصارى قالوا نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p164/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p164/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p164/r2.claim: Qatada defines the fatil as the thread in the cleft of a date stone.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p164/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا يظلمون فتيلا ﴾ قال الفتيل الذي في شق النواة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r4.claim: Fatīl is an intensive passive form, explained either as the thread in a date pit's cleft or dirt rubbed from between the fingers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r4.anchor: الفتيل: فعيل بمعنى مفعول. فقيل: هو الخيط الذي في شق نواة التمرة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r5.claim: Another explanation of fatīl is the dirt that comes off between the palms and fingers when rubbed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: ما خرج من الوسخ من بين كفيك وأصبعيك إذا فتلتهما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p671/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p671/r9.speaker: الجمهور والحسن وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p671/r9.claim: The majority identify those who praise themselves as Jews; al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd identify them as Christians.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p671/r9.anchor: قال الجمهور: هم اليهود. وقال الحسن وابن زيد: هم النصارى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r1.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r1.claim: They report that Marhab ibn Zayd, Bahri ibn Amr, and other Jews brought children to Muhammad and asked whether they were sinful; after he said no, they claimed their own sins were similarly erased, prompting the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r1.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي في آخرين: أتى مرحب بن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r2.claim: Another explanation is that they claimed to be God's sons and beloved ones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو قولهم: نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r3.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد وأبو مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r3.claim: They say the Jews presented prepubescent children as prayer leaders, claiming the sinless children would secure forgiveness for the adults praying behind them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r3.anchor: قال عكرمة، ومجاهد، وأبو مالك: كانوا يقدمون الصبيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r4.speaker: قتادة والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r4.claim: They explain the self-praise as claims that Jews or Christians are God's beloved children and that only Jews or Christians enter Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة والحسن: هو قولهم: نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r5.claim: The verse censures people who verbally praise themselves by claiming exceptional obedience, piety, and nearness to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r5.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على الغض ممن يزكي نفسه بلسانه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari cites the Prophet's assertion that he was trustworthy in heaven and earth, made when hypocrites accused him of unfair distribution; God's attestation differs from self-praise or uninformed praise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r6.anchor: شهد لنفسه أو شهد له من لا يعلم. قاله الزمخشري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r7.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r7.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes purification by deeds that display virtue from speech that reports and praises virtue.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r7.anchor: قال الراغب ما ملخصه: التزكية ضربان: بالفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r8.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r8.claim: Al-Raghib says a person is forbidden to purify himself or another except in a specified circumstance, because only God knows a person's inner state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r8.anchor: وحظر أن يزكي الإنسان نفسه، بل أن يزكي غيره، إلا على وجه مخصوص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r9.claim: “Rather” shifts away from their self-praise because they are not qualified to certify themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r9.anchor: بل: إضراب عن تزكيتهم أنفسهم، إذ ليسوا أهلا لذلك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r10.claim: God alone is the authoritative purifier because He knows hidden realities; He purifies whomever He chooses by making that person pure and describing them as purified.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r10.anchor: واعلم أن المزكي هو الله تعالى، وأنه تعالى هو المعتد بتزكيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r11.claim: “A thread” denotes a tiny amount, as in the statement that God does not wrong an atom's weight; if He wrongs no tiny amount, He will wrong nothing greater.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r11.anchor: إشارة إلى أقل شيء كقوله: إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r12.claim: The comparison with the atom's weight reinforces the assurance that God wrongs nothing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r12.anchor: كقوله: إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r13.claim: The pronoun may refer to those praising themselves or, by sense, to the chosen person; Abu Hayyan prefers the latter as nearest, while Ibn Atiyya gives the broader option of both groups mentioned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p672/r13.anchor: وجوزوا أن يعود الضمير في: ولا يظلمون، إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p677/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p677/r8.speaker: الأزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p677/r8.claim: Al-Azhari says fatil, naqir, and qitmir are proverbial for something trivial; using tiny objects in both verse endings creates a fitting parallel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p677/r8.anchor: وقال الأزهري: الفتيل والنقير، والقطمير، يضرب مثلا للشيء التافه الحقير،

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse concerns Jews who brought their children to the Prophet, asked whether the children sinned, then claimed their day and night sins were alternately erased.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي : نزلت في رجال من اليهود أتوا رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بأطفالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r2.claim: Al-Tabari reports al-Hasan's view that Jews and Christians claimed to be God's children and beloved and that only their communities would enter Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن الحسن أنها نزلت في اليهود والنصارى حيث قالوا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r3.claim: The address bids the listener wonder at their claim to purity despite disbelief and grave sin, or their claim that God erases their day and night sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r3.anchor: والمعنى انظر إليهم وتعجب من ادعائهم أنهم أزكياء عند الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r4.claim: The criticism also applies to anyone praising himself without sound purpose, apart from legitimate mention of God's favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r4.anchor: وفي معناهم من زكى نفسه وأثنى عليها لغير غرض صحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r5.claim: The clause overturns their self-purification and affirms God's purification of deserving believers; it does not pivot to a charge of miserliness and envy.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r5.anchor: إبطال لتزكية أنفسهم وإثبات لتزكية الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r6.claim: The clause is coordinated with an implied statement: they do not truly purify themselves; rather, God purifies deserving servants.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r6.anchor: والجملة عطف على مقدر ينساق إليه الكلام كأنه قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r7.claim: Tazkiya means purification and removal of what is blameworthy, as in 91:9 and 9:103.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r7.anchor: وأصل التزكية التطهير والتنزيه من القبيح

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r8.claim: Fatil is the thread in the cleft of a date stone, an image for the tiniest amount, like naqir and qitmir.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r8.anchor: وهو المراد بالفتيل وهو الخيط الذي في شق النواة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو مالك والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r9.claim: Another gloss says fatil is grime that comes out between one's fingers and palm, attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas, Abu Malik, and al-Suddi.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r9.anchor: وقيل : الفتيل ما خرج بين إصبعيك وكفيك من الوسخ وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r10.claim: The clause attaches to an omitted statement: they will be punished for the heinous claim without even the slightest injustice.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r10.anchor: أي يعاقبون بتلك الفعلة الشنيعة ولا يظلمون في ذلك العقاب أدنى ظلم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r11.claim: Alternatively, the clause is circumstantial, with its pronoun referring by sense to those God purifies: they receive their full reward at the Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54/r11.anchor: وجوز أن تكون جملة ( ولا يظلمون ) في موضع الحال والضمير راجع إلى من

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54#2/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54#2/r1.claim: Another view makes the clause independent and its pronoun refer to both self-purifiers and those God purifies; neither group's punishment or reward is reduced. Al-Alusi prefers the first reading in the warning context.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54#2/r1.anchor: وقيل : هو استئناف والضمير عائد على الموصولين من زكى نفسه ومن زكاه الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p54#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54#2/r2.speaker: علي بن عيسى
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54#2/r2.claim: Fatil is accusative as a second object of “wronged”; ʿAli ibn ʿIsa also allows an accusative of specification, like “I sweated sweat.”
ALUSI-FULL:v5p54#2/r2.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى : ويحتمل أن يكون تمييزا كقولك تصببت عرقا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī says the verse concerned Jewish men Baḥrī ibn ʿAmr, al-Nuʿmān ibn Awfā, and Marḥab ibn Zayd, who brought children to the Prophet and claimed their own sins were erased each night and day, as children's were.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: نزلت في رجال من اليهود منهم بحري بن عمرو والنعمان بن أوفى ومرحب بن زيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid and ʿIkrima say they put their children forward in prayer, claiming the children had no sins; this was the self-purification meant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعكرمة: كانوا يقدمون أطفالهم في الصلاة، يزعمون أنهم لا ذنوب لهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r3.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وقتادة ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r3.claim: They say the verse concerned Jews and Christians claiming to be God's children and beloved, and that only Jews or Christians would enter Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن والضحاك وقتادة ومقاتل: نزلت في اليهود والنصارى حين قالوا نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd interprets the self-purification as people praising and sanctifying one another.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه: هو تزكية بعضهم لبعض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r5.claim: Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb reports Ibn Masʿūd describing a man who leaves home with his religion, accepts praise from someone powerless to benefit or harm him, and returns having lost his religion; Ibn Masʿūd recited this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r5.anchor: روى طارق بن شهاب عن ابن مسعود قال: إن الرجل ليغدو من بيته ومعه دينه فيأتي الرجل لا يملك له ولا لنفسه ضرا ولا نفعا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r6.claim: God's purifying means cleansing and acquitting whom He wills of sins and setting that person right.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r6.anchor: أي: يطهر ويبرئ من الذنوب ويصلح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r7.claim: Fatil is the fiber in a date stone's groove; qitmir is its thin covering, and naqir is the small mark on its back. Alternatively, fatil is the dirt rolled between fingers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p233#2/r7.anchor: وهو اسم لما في شق النواة، والقطمير اسم للقشرة التي على النواة، والنقير اسم للنقطة التي على ظهر النواة

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r1.claim: Those who praise themselves are the People of the Book, who claimed to be God’s children and beloved.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r1.anchor: يعني أهل الكتاب قالوا نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r2.claim: A report says some Jews brought their children to the Prophet and asked if they sinned; they claimed their day and night’s sins canceled each other.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r2.anchor: ناس من اليهود جاؤوا بأطفالهم إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r3.claim: The rebuke also applies generally to anyone who self-praises and commends themselves.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r3.anchor: وفي معناهم من زكى نفسه وأثنى عليها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r4.claim: Only God’s approval counts, since He knows the good and bad concealed within people; He condemned these claimants and praised His approved believers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r4.anchor: تنبيه على أن تزكيته تعالى هي المعتد بها دون تزكية غيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r5.claim: The root sense of tazkiya is removing what is reprehensible in action or speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r5.anchor: وأصل التزكية نفي ما يستقبح فعلا أو قولا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r6.claim: They will not be wronged through blame or punishment for their unjustified self-praise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r6.anchor: بالذم أو العقاب على تزكيتهم أنفسهم بغير حق.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r7.claim: A fatīl is a tiny thread in a date stone’s cleft, proverbial for the least and smallest injustice.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:49/r7.anchor: أدنى ظلم وأصغره، وهو الخيط الذي في شق النواة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r1.claim: The people rebuked are the People of the Book, who claimed to be the most rightly guided while falsely purifying themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r1.anchor: المرادين بهذه الآيات من أهل الكتاب أضل الناس

BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r2.claim: Their false claims include that the Fire will touch them only a few days, that only Jews or Christians enter Paradise, that they deserve praise for deeds not done, and that believers should follow their desires.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r2.anchor: من قولهم ^ ( { لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودة } ) ^

BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r3.claim: Only God purifies, by His complete knowledge, power, wisdom, and justice, praising a person and creating good qualities that produce righteous deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r3.anchor: بما له من العلم التام والقدرة الشاملة والحكمة البالغة والعدل السوي بالثناء عليه وبخلق معاني الخير

BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r4.claim: A person whom God has purified in a capacity such as prophethood may declare that status to convey what benefits people from God.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r4.anchor: فإذا زكى أحدا من أصفيائه بشيء كالنبوة , كان له أن يزكي نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r5.claim: Fatīl is the tiny twisted thread in a date stone’s cleft; it stands for neither slight nor great injustice.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r5.anchor: في شق النواة من ذلك الشيء المفتول , أي قليلا ولا كثيرا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r6.claim: God wrongs no one because He knows what each deserves, is the just judge, and has no need to oppress.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r6.anchor: لأنه عالم بما يستحقون وهو الحكم العدل الغني عن الظلم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r7.claim: The inimitability of God’s speech in both elaboration and concision proves the People of the Book’s falsehood, sharpening the rebuke that follows.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p266/r7.anchor: الإعجاز في حالتي الإطناب والإيجاز ؛ ثبت كذبهم

BURSEVI:v2p174/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p174/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p174/r8.claim: The address to the Prophet expresses amazement at Jews who claim purity from sin and say they are God's children and beloved, despite their disbelief and grave sins.
BURSEVI:v2p174/r8.anchor: خطاب للنبي عليه السلام على وجه التعجيب

BURSEVI:v2p174/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p174/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p174/r9.claim: The wording also warns anyone who boasts of exceptional piety, obedience, or closeness to God against admiring their own deeds.
BURSEVI:v2p174/r9.anchor: واللفظ عام يشتمل كل من زكى نفسه ووصفها بزيادة التقوى والطاعة والزلفى عند الله

BURSEVI:v2p174/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p174/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p174/r10.claim: Only God truly purifies those among His believing servants who merit it, since He knows the good and evil concealed within a person.
BURSEVI:v2p174/r10.anchor: تزكيته ممن يستأهلها من المرتضين من عباده المؤمنين

BURSEVI:v2p174/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p174/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p174/r11.claim: A fatil is the tiny thread in a date stone's cleft, a proverbial measure for the least possible injustice; injustice would add to punishment or subtract from reward.
BURSEVI:v2p174/r11.anchor: وهو الخيط الذي في شق النواة يضرب به المثل في القلة والحقارة

BURSEVI:v2p174/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p174/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p174/r12.claim: They are not wronged by the punishment they receive for their ugly deed.
BURSEVI:v2p174/r12.anchor: أي يعاقبون بتلك الفعلة القبيحة ولا يظلمون في ذلك العقاب

DURR-FULL:v2p559/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Jews claimed their deceased children were close to God, would intercede for them, and would purify them.
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن اليهود قالوا: إن أبناءنا قد توفوا وهم لنا قربة عند الله وسيشفعون لنا ويزكوننا

DURR-FULL:v2p559/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Jews presented children as prayer leaders and offerings, claiming they had no sins; God says a sinner is not purified through another person's innocence.
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كانت اليهود يقدمون صبيانهم يصلون بهم ويقربون قربانهم ويزعمون أنهم لا خطايا لهم ولا ذنوب

DURR-FULL:v2p559/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r5.claim: Mujāhid identifies the self-purifiers as Jews who put their children at the front of prayer and made them lead, claiming they were sinless.
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم} قال: يعني يهود كانوا يقدمون صبيانا لهم أمامهم في الصلاة فيؤمونهم

DURR-FULL:v2p559/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r6.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r6.claim: Abū Mālik says the verse was revealed about Jews who put their children forward, claiming that the children had no sins.
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r6.anchor: عن أبي مالك في قوله {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم} قال: نزلت في اليهود كانوا يقدمون صبيانهم يقولون: ليست لهم ذنوب

DURR-FULL:v2p559/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r7.claim: ʿIkrima says the People of the Book put prepubescent boys forward to lead prayer, claiming they had no sins.
DURR-FULL:v2p559/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: كان أهل الكتاب يقدمون الغلمان الذين لم يبلغوا الحنث يصلون بهم يقولون: ليس لهم ذنوب

DURR-FULL:v2p560/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Jews and Christians claimed to be God's children and beloved, and claimed that only Jews or Christians would enter Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم} قال: هم اليهود والنصارى (قالوا نحن أبناء الله واحباؤه)

DURR-FULL:v2p560/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says Jews claimed that teaching their sons Torah while young left them sinless, and that their daytime sins were forgiven at night.
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r2.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم} قال: نزلت في اليهود قالوا: إنا نعلم أبناءنا التوراة صغارا فلا يكون لهم ذنوب

DURR-FULL:v2p560/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd warns that someone may betray his religion, flatter a person who cannot help or harm him, gain nothing, and incur God's anger; he then recites this verse.
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: إن الرجل ليغدر بدينه ثم يرجع وما معه منه شيء يلقى الرجل ليس يملك له نفعا ولا ضرا

DURR-FULL:v2p560/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses fatīl as what comes out when something is rubbed between the fingers, stressing the tiny amount by which no one is wronged.
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ولا يظلمون فتيلا} قال: الفتيل: ما خرج من بين الأصبعين

DURR-FULL:v2p560/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās distinguishes the naqīr as the date pit's indentation, the fatīl as the thread along its cleft, and the quṭmīr as its thin covering.
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: النقير: النقرة تكون في النواة التي تنبت منها النخلة والفتيل: الذي يكون على شق النواة والقطمير: القشر الذي يكون على النواة

DURR-FULL:v2p560/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that people will not lose even a thread's worth of good or evil; it lies in the cleft of a date stone.
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله عز وجل {ولا يظلمون فتيلا} قال: لا ينقصون من الخير والشر مثل الفتيل

DURR-FULL:v2p560/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r7.speaker: النابغة الذبياني
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r7.claim: Al-Nābigha ibn Dhubyān's verse uses fatīl for a negligible amount, illustrating the Arabic expression cited by Ibn ʿAbbās.
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r7.anchor: نابغة بني ذبيان يقول: يجمع الجيش ذا الألوف ويغزو ثم لا يرزأ الأعادي فتيلا

DURR-FULL:v2p560/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r8.claim: Mujāhid locates the naqīr in the seed's back, the fatīl within its cleft or as grime rubbed off, and the quṭmīr as its wrapping, an egg membrane, or reed skin.
DURR-FULL:v2p560/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: النقير: الذي يكون في وسط النواة في ظهرها والفتيل: الذي يكون في جوف النواة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jews had their children lead prayers and offer sacrifices, claiming they had no sins; the verse was revealed to reject that claim. Mujahid, Abu Malik, al-Suddi, Ikrimah, and al-Dahhak are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كانت اليهود يقدمون صبيانهم يصلون بهم ، ويقربون قربانهم ، ويزعمون انهم لا خطايا لهم ولا ذنوب

IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r2.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the self-purifiers as Jews and Christians, who claimed to be God's children and beloved and said only Jews or Christians would enter Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : الم تر إلى الذين يزكون انفسهم قال : هم اليهود والنصارى قالوا : نحن ابناء الله واحباؤه

IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the Jews claimed they had no sins, just as their ancestors had no sins, and that this verse was revealed about them.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك : اما قوله : الم تر إلى الذين يزكون انفسهم فان اليهود قالوا : ليس لنا ذنوب

IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God does not purify a sinner by means of someone else who has no sin.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : بل الله يزكي من يشاء قال الله تعالى : اني لا اطهر ذا ذنب باخر لا ذنب له

IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the fatīl as what is twisted between two fingers; Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Malik, and al-Suddi are also reported with this gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ولا يظلمون فتيلا قال : الفتيل : ما فتل بين الاصبعين

IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r6.claim: A second gloss from Ibn Abbas identifies the fatīl as the line in the groove on a date stone.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p972/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس ولا يظلمون فتيلا يعني : الذي في الشق الذي في بطن النواة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p973/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p973/r1.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v3p973/r1.claim: Ata defines the fatīl as the thin line inside a date stone; al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Atiyya al-Awfi, Khasif, and Qatada are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p973/r1.anchor: عن عطاء قال : الفتيل : الذي في بطن النواة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r1.claim: The rebuke targets Jews who claim to be God's children and beloved and say that only Jews will enter Paradise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r1.anchor: تعجيب من حال اليهود إذ يقولون { نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r2.claim: Divine purification, not self-praise, is God's testimony; the claim that God purifies whom He wills directly overturns their self-certification.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r3.claim: The particle bal explicitly repudiates their claim; without it, they could still hope to be among those God purifies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r3.anchor: تصدير الجملة ب ( بل ) تصريح بإبطال تزكيتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r4.claim: God has not denied them what they deserve, and purifying others does not wrong them, because God speaks truth and guides the way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r4.anchor: أي أن الله لم يحرمهم ما هم به أحرياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r5.claim: Fatīl is like a thread in the groove of a date stone; it became a metaphor for a tiny amount because it is useless and barely visible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r5.anchor: والفتيل : شبه خيط في شق نواة التمرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r6.claim: Fatīlan stands in place of an absolute object, with the comparison particle omitted: no injustice equivalent to a thread; compare 4:40.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p84#2/r6.anchor: وانتصب { فتيلا } على النيابة عن المفعول المطلق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r1.speaker: المتأولون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r1.claim: Although the wording is general, interpreters unanimously identify the people who claim self-purification as Jews.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r1.anchor: هذا لفظ عام في ظاهره، ولم يختلف أحد من المتأولين في أن المراد اليهود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r2.speaker: قتادة والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r2.claim: Qatada and al-Hasan say the Jews’ self-praise was claiming to be God’s children and beloved, and claiming only Jews enter Paradise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r2.anchor: فقال قتادة والحسن: ذلك قولهم نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi say they claimed to be sinless: daytime sins were forgiven at night, nighttime sins by day, and they were like children.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي: ذلك قولهم: لا ذنوب لنا وما فعلناه نهارا غفر ليلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مالك وعكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r4.claim: Mujahid, Abu Malik, and ʿIkrima say they put their young children forward to lead prayer because the children had no sins; Ibn ʿAtiyya considers this remote from the verse’s aim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد وأبو مالك وعكرمة: تقديمهم أولادهم الصغار للصلاة لأنهم لا ذنوب لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the explanation about presenting children for prayer is remote from the verse’s purpose.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says they claimed their deceased sons would intercede for them and purify them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ذلك قولهم أبناؤنا الذين ماتوا يشفعون لنا ويزكوننا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud says their self-purification consisted of praising and extolling one another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r7.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود: ذلك ثناء بعضهم على بعض، ومدحهم لهم وتزكيتهم لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r8.claim: The verse rebukes people who praise themselves verbally: true purity belongs to those whose deeds are good and whom God purifies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r8.anchor: فتقتضي هذه الآية الغض من المزكي لنفسه بلسانه، والإعلام بأن الزاكي المزكى من حسنت أفعاله وزكاه الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r9.claim: The pronoun in “they are not wronged” refers to the previously mentioned self-purifying people or those whom God purifies; God’s justice is already known independently of this verse for others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r9.anchor: والضمير في يزكون عائد على المذكورين ممن زكى نفسه أو ممن يزكيه الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r10.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r10.claim: A group reads the verb with second-person tāʾ, “you are not wronged,” instead of third-person yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r10.anchor: وقرأت طائفة «ولا تظلمون» بالتاء على الخطاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r11.claim: Fatīl derives from twisting and has the form faʿīl with the sense of mafʿūl, something twisted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r11.anchor: هو ما فتل، فهو فعيل بمعنى مفعول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء ومجاهد وغيرهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtaʾ, Mujahid, and others define fatīl as the thread in the cleft of a date stone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعطاء ومجاهد وغيرهم: «الفتيل» : الخيط الذي في شق نواة التمرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو مالك والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Abu Malik, and al-Suddi define fatīl as the residue between the fingers or palms when rubbed; both definitions signify something negligible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وأبو مالك والسدي: هو ما خرج من بين إصبعيك أو كفيك إذا فتلتهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r14.claim: The word fatīlan is the second object of the verb “wrong.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p65#2/r14.anchor: ونصبه على مفعول ثان ب يظلمون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says two Jewish men, Marḥab ibn Zayd and Baḥrī ibn ʿAwn, brought their children and other Jews to ask whether the children had sins; after the Prophet said no, they claimed they were just like them, with sins committed by day expiated by night and vice versa, and the verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r1.anchor: أن مرحب ابن زيد وبحري بن عون وهما من اليهود أتيا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأطفالهما ومعهما طائفة من اليهود فقالوا يا محمد هل على هؤلاء من ذنب قال لا قالوا والله ما نحن إلا كهيئتهم ما من ذنب نعمله بالنهار إلا كفر عنا بالليل وما من ذنب نعمله بالليل إلا كفر عنا بالنهار فنزلت هذه الآية هذا قول ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says alam tara means “have you been informed?”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r2.anchor: قولان أحدهما ألم تخبر قاله ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says alam tara means “have you known?”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r4.claim: One identification of those who purify themselves is the Jews, as in Ibn ʿAbbās's account.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r4.anchor: أحدهما اليهود على ما ذكرنا عن ابن عباس وبه قال مجاهد وقتادة ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r5.speaker: الحسن، ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r5.claim: Another identification is both Jews and Christians.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r5.anchor: والثاني أنهم اليهود والنصارى وبه قال الحسن وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r6.claim: They claim to be pure; the root can describe something growing in righteousness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r6.anchor: ومعنى يزكون أنفسهم يزعمون أنهم أزكياء يقال زكى الشيء إذا نما في الصلاح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r7.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r7.claim: One account says they absolved themselves of sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r7.anchor: أحدها أنهم برؤوا أنفسهم من الذنوب رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r8.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r8.claim: Another account says Jews claimed their deceased children would purify them before God and intercede for them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r8.anchor: والثاني أن اليهود قالوا إن أبناءنا الذين ماتوا يزكوننا عند الله ويشفعون لنا رواه عطية عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r9.speaker: عكرمة، مجاهد، أبو مالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r9.claim: A third account says Jews put children forward to lead prayer, claiming the children had no sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r9.anchor: والثالث أن اليهود كانوا يقدمون صبيانهم في الصلاة فيؤمونهم يزعمون أنهم لا ذنوب لهم هذا قول عكرمة ومجاهد وأبي مالك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r10.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p104/r10.claim: A fourth account says Jews and Christians claimed “We are God's children and beloved” and that only Jews or Christians would enter Paradise.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r1.claim: God makes pure whomever He wills, and wrongs no one by even the amount of a fatil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r1.anchor: يجعله زاكيا ولا يظلم الله أحدا مقدار فتيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r2.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r2.claim: Ibn Jarir says fatil derives from maftul, shifted from the passive-participle pattern to faʿil, like sariʿ and dahin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r2.anchor: قال ابن جرير وأصل الفتيل المفتول صرف عن مفعول إلى فعيل كصريع ودهين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r3.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس، مجاهد، عطاء بن أبي رباح، الضحاك، قتادة، عطية، ابن زيد، مقاتل، أبو عبيدة، ابن قتيبة، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r3.claim: One view takes fatil as the fiber in the groove of a date stone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r3.anchor: أنه ما يكون في شق النواة رواه عكرمة عن ابن عباس وبه قال مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r4.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير، أبو مالك، السدي، الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r4.claim: A second view takes fatil as dirt that emerges between the fingers when they are rubbed together.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p105/r4.anchor: أنه ما يخرج بين الأصابع من الوسخ إذا دلكن رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say the verse concerns Jews and Christians who claimed to be God's sons and beloved ones.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r1.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة: نزلت هذه الآية، وهي قوله: {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم} في اليهود والنصارى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd connects the verse both to their claim to be God's sons and beloved ones and to their claim that only Jews or Christians enter Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r2.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: نزلت في قولهم: {نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه} [المائدة:18]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r3.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة، أبو مالك، السدي، الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r3.claim: Mujahid says they put children forward to lead prayers and supplications, claiming the children had no sins; Ikrima and Abu Malik agree, and Mujahid, Abu Malik, al-Suddi, Ikrima, and al-Dahhak are also reported to give similar accounts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كانوا يقدمون الصبيان أمامهم في الدعاء والصلاة يؤمونهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r4.claim: Al-Awfi reports Ibn Abbas's explanation that Jews said their deceased children were a means of nearness and would intercede for and purify them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم} وذلك أن اليهود قالوا: إن أبناءنا توفوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r5.claim: In a report through Ikrima, Ibn Abbas says Jews had children lead prayers and made offerings, claiming the children had no sins.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس قال: كانت اليهود يقدمون صبيانهم يصلون بهم، ويقربون قربانهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects the Jews' claim that their children were sinless and says God does not purify a sinner through someone else's innocence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r6.anchor: ويزعمون أنهم لا خطايا لهم ولا ذنوب. وكذبوا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says they claimed to have no sins, just as their children had no sins, and the verse was revealed concerning them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r7.anchor: وقال الضحاك: قالوا: ليس لنا ذنوب، كما ليس لأبنائنا ذنوب. فأنزل الله ذلك فيهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r8.claim: An unnamed view takes the verse as condemning excessive mutual praise and self-purification.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r8.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في ذم التمادح والتزكية.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r9.claim: In a sound report in Muslim, the Prophet instructed that dirt be thrown in the faces of people who lavish praise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r9.anchor: عن المقداد بن الأسود قال: أمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن نحثو في وجوه المداحين التراب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r10.claim: In a report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections, the Prophet called a flatterer's praise destructive and advised saying I think him so, since no one should declare another pure before God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332/r10.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة، عن أبيه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سمع رجلا يثني على رجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r1.claim: Ahmad reports Umar saying that whoever declares himself a believer is an unbeliever, whoever calls himself learned is ignorant, and whoever says he is in Paradise is in Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r1.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب: من قال: أنا مؤمن، فهو كافر. ومن قال: هو عالم، فهو جاهل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r2.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r2.claim: A second report from Umar calls self-admiration the thing he most fears for people and repeats the warning against declaring oneself a believer, learned, or Paradise-bound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r2.anchor: عن عمر أنه قال: إن أخوف ما أخاف عليكم إعجاب المرء برأيه، فمن قال: إنه مؤمن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r3.speaker: معاوية عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r3.claim: Muawiya transmitted that God grants understanding of religion to whom He wills, lawful wealth is blessed, and excessive praise is destructive; Ibn Majah transmits the final warning alone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r3.anchor: عن معبد الجهني قال: كان معاوية قلما يحدث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies Maʿbad as Maʿbad ibn Abd Allah ibn Uwaym, a Basran Qadari.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r4.anchor: ومعبد هذا هو ابن عبد الله بن عويم البصري القدري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud warns that a person may lose his religion by praising someone unable to benefit or harm him, gaining nothing and earning God's anger; he then recited the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r5.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن قيس بن مسلم، عن طارق بن شهاب قال: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: إن الرجل ليغدو بدينه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r6.claim: God alone determines who is purified because He knows the realities and hidden aspects of all matters.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p332#2/r6.anchor: ولهذا قال تعالى: {بل الله يزكي من يشاء} أي: المرجع في ذلك إلى الله، عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p333/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p333/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، عكرمة، عطاء، الحسن، قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p333/r1.claim: These early authorities explain the fitil as the fine thread in the cleft of a date stone; the verse promises that no reward, however tiny, is withheld.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p333/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وعكرمة، وعطاء، والحسن، وقتادة، وغير واحد من السلف: هو ما يكون في شق النواة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p333/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p333/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p333/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also defines fitil as what one twists between the fingers; Ibn Kathir says the two explanations are close.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p333/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا: هو ما فتلت بين أصابعك. وكلا القولين متقارب.

JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r1.claim: Tazkiya means purification and sanctification; describing someone as pure can itself be tazkiya.
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r1.anchor: التزكية: التطهير والتقديس، وقد يكون الوصف بالتطهير تزكية.

JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r2.claim: Fatil comes from twisting; a fatila is a wick and fatil means something twisted.
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r2.anchor: والفتل: لي الشيء، فتلت الحبل أفتله فتلا. وانفتل فلان في صلاته، والفتيلة معروفة، والفتيل بمعنى مفتول،

JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses fatil in a line about attaining the speaker's glory.
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر: يا أيها الساعي ليدرك مجدنا ... ثكلتك أمك أن ترد فتيلا

JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r4.claim: Nazar is turning attention; it can be physical, intellectual, merciful, hostile, expectant, or argumentative, while ru'ya is perception.
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r4.anchor: والنظر: الإقبال على الشيء بالبصر فمنه النظر بالقلب، لأنه إقبال عليه كالإقبال بالبصر،

JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r5.claim: Seeing with the eye turns the pupil toward an object; reflection is considering a thing.
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r5.anchor: والنظر بالعين تقليب الحدقة نحو المرئي التماسا لرؤيته مع سلامة الحاسة، والنظر بالتقلب: التفكر في الشيء،

JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r8.claim: Fatil is an object meaning the measure of a fatil; another parsing treats it as specification.
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r8.anchor: نصب فتيلا لأنه مفعول تقديره: لا يظلمون مقدار فتيل

JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r10.speaker: السلمي
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r10.claim: Al-Sulami reads tara with still ra, a dialect after deleting the jussive letter; the open form is more elevated.
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r10.anchor: وعن السلمي بسكون الراء، وهي لغة قوم لا يكتفون من الجزم بحذف الحرف حتى سكنوا حركته، والأول اللغة العالية.

JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r11.speaker: الكلبي
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r11.claim: Al-Kalbi says this came down about Jewish men who brought children to the Prophet, asked if they were sinful, and claimed day and night sins canceled; God exposed them.
JISHUMI:v2p1586#2/r11.anchor: قيل: نزلت في رجال من اليهود أتوا بأطفال لهم إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وقالوا: يا محمد هل على هؤلاء ذنب؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r1.claim: The people who praise themselves are Jews and Christians, who claimed to be God’s children and beloved and said only Jews or Christians would enter Paradise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r1.anchor: اليهود والنصارى قالوا نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r2.claim: An unattributed report says Jewish men brought their children to the Prophet, who said the children had no sin; they claimed their own daytime sins were erased at night and nighttime sins by day, and the verse was revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r2.anchor: بأطفالهم فقالوا هل على هؤلاء ذنب قال ( لا )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r3.claim: The warning includes anyone who declares their own deeds, obedience, piety, or nearness to God pure and superior.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r3.anchor: ويدخل فيها كل من زكى نفسه ووصفها بزكاء العمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r4.claim: The Prophet’s statement that he was trustworthy in heaven and earth came after hypocrites demanded fair division, refuting their accusation that he acted unlike God’s description of him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p552/r4.anchor: إنما قال ذلك حين قال له المنافقون اعدل في القسمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r1.claim: Only God’s purification counts, since He knows who deserves it; He purifies approved servants whom He recognizes as pure and describes accordingly.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r1.anchor: اعلام بأن تزكية الله هي التي يعتد بها لا تزكية غيره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r2.claim: God purifies servants He approves, recognizing their purity and describing them by it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r2.anchor: يزكي المرتضين من عباده الذين عرف منهم الزكاء فوصفهم به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r3.claim: One possible sense is that self-praisers receive the full measure of punishment they deserve for praising themselves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r3.anchor: أي الذين يزكون أنفسهم يعاقبون على تزكيتهم أنفسهم حق جزائهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r4.claim: Alternatively, those whom God purifies receive the full reward for their purity, with none of it diminished.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r4.anchor: أو من يشاء يثابون على زكائهم ولا ينقص من ثوابهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r5.claim: This echoes the prohibition on self-praise because God knows best who is pious.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p553/r5.anchor: فلا تزكوا أنفسكم هو أعلم بمن اتقى

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r1.speaker: قتادة، الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r1.claim: The Jews' self-purification refers to their claim that they are God's children and beloved by Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r1.anchor: قولهم نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه , وهذا قول قتادة , والحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r2.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r2.claim: They presented their children to lead prayer, claiming that the children had no sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r2.anchor: تقديمهم أطفالهم لإمامتهم زعما منهم أنه لا ذنوب لهم , وهذا قول مجاهد , وعكرمة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r3.claim: They claimed that their children would seek forgiveness for them and purify them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r3.anchor: هو قولهم إن أبناءنا يستغفرون لنا ويزكوننا , وهذا قول ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r4.claim: Some Jews praised one another to obtain worldly advantage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r4.anchor: تزكية بعضهم لبعض لينالوا به شيئا من الدنيا , وهذا قول ابن مسعود .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r5.speaker: عطاء، قتادة، مجاهد، الحسن، ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r5.claim: Fitil is the thread or groove split in a date stone; these authorities, including one view of Ibn Abbas, identify it this way.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r5.anchor: الفتيل الذي شق النواة , وهو قول عطاء , وقتادة , ومجاهد , والحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r6.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r6.claim: Hasan locates the fitil inside the date stone, the naqir on its back, and the qitmir as its skin.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r6.anchor: قال الحسن : الفتيل ما في بطن النواة , والنقير ما في ظهرها , والقطمير قشرها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r7.speaker: السدي، ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r7.claim: Another view identifies fitil as dirt rolled between the fingers; this is also one view of Ibn Abbas.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p494/r7.anchor: أنه ما انفتل بين الأصابع من الوسخ , وهذا قول السدي , وأحد قولي ابن عباس .

MUJAHID:v1p160#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p160#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p160#3/r1.claim: The Jews advanced their boys to lead prayer, claiming the children had no sins; Mujahid identifies this as their self-purification.
MUJAHID:v1p160#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم ﴾ قال هم اليهود كانوا يقدمون صبيانهم في الصلوة فيؤمونهم

MUQATIL:4:49-51/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r1.claim: The opening asks, “Do you not look?”; Muqātil glosses the following “to” as “action.”
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r1.anchor: { ألم تر } ، يعنى ألم تنظر { إلى } ، يعنى فعل

MUQATIL:4:49-51/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r2.claim: The self-purifiers are Jews, including Baḥrī b. ʿAmr and Marḥab b. Zayd, who brought their sons to the Prophet and asked whether they had sins.
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r2.anchor: { الذين يزكون أنفسهم } ، يعنى اليهود، منهم بحرى بن عمرو، ومرحب بن زيد، دخلوا بأولادهم إلى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم،

MUQATIL:4:49-51/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r3.claim: After the Prophet said the sons had no sins, the Jews claimed to be God's sons and beloved, with every day's sins forgiven by the next night or day.
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r3.anchor: فقالوا: والذى تحلف به ما نحن إلا كهيئتهم، نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه، وما من ذنب نعمله بالنهار إلا غفر لنا بالليل،

MUQATIL:4:49-51/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r4.claim: God purifies means that He reforms whichever of His servants He wills.
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r4.anchor: { بل الله يزكى من يشاء } ، يعنى يصلح من يشاء من عباده،

MUQATIL:4:49-51/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r5.claim: A fatīl is the white fiber in the groove of a date stone; no one is deprived even of this tiny measure of deeds.
MUQATIL:4:49-51/r5.anchor: { ولا يظلمون } ، يعنى ولا ينقصون من أعمالهم { فتيلا } [آية: 49]، يعنى الأبيض الذى يكون فى شق النواة من الفتيل.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.claim: The rebuke includes anyone who praises their own purity of deeds, abundant obedience, or piety.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.anchor: ويدخل فيها كل من زكى نفسه ووصفها بزكاء العمل وزيادة الطاعة والتقوى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.claim: Only God's assessment of purity counts, because He knows who merits it; the author links this to the command not to praise oneself in 53:32.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.anchor: إعلام بأن تزكية الله هى التى يعتدبها لا تزكية غيره لأنه هو العالم بمن هو أهل للتزكية ونحوه فلا تزكوا أنفسكم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.claim: The phrase may mean self-praisers receive the full just recompense for their self-praise, or that those God purifies receive their full reward.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.anchor: أى الذين يزكون أنفسهم يعاقبون على تزكية أنفسهم حق جزائهم أو من يشاء يثابون على زكائهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.claim: A fatīl is the tiny trace of dirt produced by rubbing the fingers together.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.anchor: قدر فتيل وهو ما يحدث بفتل الأصابع من الوسخ

QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r8.claim: Although the wording is general, exegetes unanimously identify its referent as the Jews.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r8.anchor: هذا اللفظ عام في ظاهره ولم يختلف أحد من المتأولين في أن المراد اليهود.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r9.speaker: قتادة والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r9.claim: Qatada and al-Hasan say they claimed to be God’s children and beloved, and that only Jews or Christians enter Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r9.anchor: فقال قتادة والحسن: ذلك قولهم: { نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه }

QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r10.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi say they claimed no sins, that day’s sins were forgiven at night and night’s by day, and they were like children.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r10.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي: قولهم لا ذنوب لنا وما فعلناه نهارا غفر لنا ليلا وما فعلناه ليلا غفر لنا نهارا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r11.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مالك وعكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r11.claim: They say Jews put children forward to pray because the children had no sins; al-Qurtubi says this is far from the verse’s purpose.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد وأبو مالك وعكرمة: تقديمهم الصغار للصلاة لأنهم لا ذنوب عليهم. وهذا يبعد من مقصد الآية.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says they claimed their deceased forefathers would intercede for and purify them.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ذلك قولهم آباؤنا الذين ماتوا يشفعون لنا ويزكوننا.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r13.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r13.claim: Ibn Masʿud says they praised one another; al-Qurtubi prefers this as the verse’s apparent meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r13.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود: ذلك ثناء بعضهم على بعض. وهذا أحسن ما قيل فإنه الظاهر من معنى الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:48-49/r14.claim: Tazkiya means purification and declaring oneself free of sins.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r1.claim: Read with 53:32, the verse censures self-praise: real purity lies in good deeds and God’s approval, not one’s appraisal.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r1.anchor: فلا تزكوا أنفسكم [النجم: 32] يقتضي الغض من المزكي لنفسه بلسانه، والإعلام بأن الزاكي المزكى من حسنت أفعاله

QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r2.claim: In Muslim’s report through Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAta, Zaynab bint Abi Salama recounts that the Prophet rejected the name Barrah, saying people should not declare themselves pious, and renamed her Zaynab.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r2.anchor: فقالت لي زينب بنت أبي سلمة: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى عن هذا الاسم، وسميت برة فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r3.claim: Scripture and Sunna prohibit self-praise; Egyptian titles implying purity have often been emptied of meaning by their bearers’ vices.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r3.anchor: فقد دل الكتاب والسنة على المنع من تزكية الإنسان نفسه، ويجري هذا المجرى ما قد كثر في هذه الديار المصرية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r4.claim: In Bukhari’s report from Abu Bakra, after someone praised a man the Prophet warned against cutting his neck with praise and advised qualified praise while leaving his standing to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r4.anchor: أن رجلا ذكر عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأثنى عليه رجل خيرا، فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ويحك قطعت عنق صاحبك يقوله مرارا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r5.claim: False excess praise can cause vanity and inflated self-regard, leading to neglected deeds and failure to seek virtue; another report says it breaks a man’s back.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r5.anchor: فنهى صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يفرط في مدح الرجل بما ليس فيه فيدخله في ذلك الإعجاب والكبر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r6.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r6.claim: Scholars read ‘throw dust in the faces of eulogists’ as condemning false flatterers who exploit and delude people, not honest praise intended to encourage good deeds; intention matters.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:44-53/r6.anchor: أن المراد به المداحون في وجوههم بالباطل وبما ليس فيهم، حتى يجعلوا ذلك بضاعة يستأكلون به الممدوح

QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r2.claim: The Prophet was praised in poetry, speeches, and conversation without rebuke by Abu Talib, al-ʿAbbas, Hassan, and Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr; he also praised his Companions for their conduct under greed and danger.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r2.anchor: وقد مدح صلى الله عليه وسلم في الشعر والخطب والمخاطبة ولم يحث في وجوه المداحين التراب، ولا أمر بذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r3.claim: The Prophet forbids exaggerating his praise as Christians exaggerated Jesus, instructing people to call him God’s servant and messenger.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r3.anchor: لا تطروني كما أطرت النصارى عيسى ابن مريم وقولوا: عبد الله ورسوله

QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r4.claim: The hadith means not to attribute qualities the Prophet lacks to praise him; Christians did this by claiming Jesus was God’s son and disbelieved.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r4.anchor: فمعناه لا تصفوني بما ليس في من الصفات تلتمسون بذلك مدحي، كما وصفت النصارى عيسى بما لم يكن فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r5.claim: Raising anyone beyond their proper rank through qualities they lack is sinful; had this been permissible, the Prophet would have been most entitled to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r5.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن من رفع امرا فوق حده وتجاوز مقداره بما ليس فيه فمعتد آثم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r6.claim: The pronoun refers to both those who purify themselves and those whom God purifies; God’s justice toward others is established elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r6.anchor: الضمير في «يظلمون» عائد على المذكورين ممن زكى نفسه وممن يزكيه الله عز وجل.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r7.claim: They explain fatil as the thread in the groove of a date stone.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r7.anchor: والفتيل الخيط الذي في شق نواة التمرة قاله ابن عباس وعطاء ومجاهد.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r8.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r8.claim: Another explanation makes fatil the skin between the date stone and the fruit.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r8.anchor: وقيل: القشرة التي حول النواة بينها وبين البسرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو مالك والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r9.claim: They explain fatil as the dirt released when rubbing fingers or palms; the word is on a passive pattern.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وأبو مالك والسدي: هو ما يخرج بين أصبعيك أو كفيك من الوسخ إذا فتلتهما

QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r10.claim: All these glosses signify an insignificant amount: God does not wrong anyone by even the smallest measure.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r10.anchor: وهذا كله يرجع إلى كناية عن تحقير الشيء وتصغيره، وأن الله لا يظلمه شيئا.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r11.claim: The parallel ‘not wronged a naqir’ in 4:124 means the dimple on a date stone from which a palm grows, likewise expressing a negligible amount.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r11.anchor: ومثل هذا في التحقير قوله تعالى: ولا يظلمون نقيرا [النساء: 124] وهو النكتة التي في ظهر النواة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r12.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r12.claim: A poet uses fatil to mean the least harm: a king raises an army of thousands but does not injure the enemy by a thread’s worth.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:49-50/r12.anchor: قال الشاعر يذم بعض الملوك: تجمع الجيش ذا الألوف وتغزو ثم لا ترزأ العدو فتيلا

QASHANI:4:48-50/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:48-50/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:48-50/r2.claim: Self-purification by the self is impossible because the ego’s qualities are inherent and necessarily endure with it.

QASHANI:4:48-50/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:48-50/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:48-50/r3.claim: He cites the warning about guarding the soul from greed as evidence that vices are mixed into it and persist with it.
QASHANI:4:48-50/r3.anchor: إذ هي لوازم النفس باقية لازمة لها

QASHANI:4:48-50/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:48-50/r4.speaker: النبي
QASHANI:4:48-50/r4.claim: A Prophetic saying calls the worst person the one upon whom resurrection comes while still alive.
QASHANI:4:48-50/r4.anchor:
وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام:
" شر الناس من قامت عليه القيامة وهو حي "

QASHANI:4:48-50/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:48-50/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:48-50/r5.claim: The saying describes one who reaches knowledge of tawhid before the ego dies through annihilation and lives through God; he then becomes a heretic who permits everything.
QASHANI:4:48-50/r5.anchor: يقف على علم التوحيد ونفسه لم تمت بالفناء حتى تحيى بالله

QASHANI:4:48-50/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:48-50/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:48-50/r6.claim: God purifies whom He wills by erasing their qualities and removing them through His own attributes.

QASHANI:4:48-50/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:48-50/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:48-50/r7.claim: God does not withhold even a tiny amount of the soul’s attributes or their due: He exchanges weak, fleeting qualities for His strong, lasting attributes.
QASHANI:4:48-50/r7.anchor: فإن الله لا يأخذ شيئا منها مع ضعفها وسرعة انقضائها حتى يعطي بدله من صفاته مع قوتها ودوامها

RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r1.speaker: author
