RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r1.claim: After the threat about shirk, Jews claimed special status as God’s children and beloved, expected only brief punishment, and said only Jews or Christians enter Paradise; some relied on prophetic ancestors to intercede.
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r1.anchor: لسنا من المشركين ، بل نحن خواص الله تعالى كما حكى تعالى عنهم انه قالوا : { نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه }

RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Jews brought children to the Prophet and, after he said the children were sinless, claimed that their own day and night’s deeds canceled each other out.
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أن قوما من اليهود أتوا بأطفالهم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r3.claim: Tazkiya here means a person praising themself, like a witness being declared upright; because piety is inward and only God knows it, only God can truly purify.
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r3.anchor: التزكية في هذا الموضع عبارة عن مدح الإنسان نفسه ، ومنه تزكية المعدل للشاهد

RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r4.claim: When asked how the Prophet could call himself trustworthy in heaven and earth, Rāzī answers that he said this after hypocrites challenged his fairness and God had authenticated him by a miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r4.anchor: أليس أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( والله إني لأمين في السماء أمين في الأرض )

RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r5.claim: Since faith is the greatest and noblest purification, God’s saying that He purifies whom He wills shows that He creates believers’ faith.
RAZI-FULL:v10p102/r5.anchor: دل على أن إيمان المؤمنين لم يحصل إلا بخلق الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r1.claim: No injustice by even a thread can mean either that self-praisers receive their due punishment without injustice or that those God purifies receive their full reward.
RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r1.anchor: والمعنى ان الذين يزكون أنفسهم يعاقبون على تلك التزكية حق جزائهم من غير ظلم

RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, those whom God purifies are rewarded for their obedience without any reduction in reward.
RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r2.anchor: أن الذين زكاهم الله فإنه يثيبهم على طاعاتهم ولا ينقص من ثوابهم شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r3.claim: Fatīl can be the grime twisted between fingers; Ibn al-Sikkīt defines it as the groove in a date stone, while naqīr is its dot and quṭmīr its thin covering; all denote something tiny.
RAZI-FULL:v10p102#2/r3.anchor: وعن ابن السكيت : الفتيل ما كان في شق النواة ، والنقير النقطة التي في ظهر النواة ، والقطمير القشرة الرقيقة على النواة

STUDYQURAN:4:49/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r1.claim: Some identify Madinan Jews, but the author considers the People of the Book generally the more likely referent.
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r1.anchor: These verses continue the criticism of the Madinan Jews (Q) or more likely of the People of the Book in general (Z)

STUDYQURAN:4:49/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r2.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r2.claim: Most commentators connect the purity claims to assertions that Jews or the People of the Book are God’s children and beloved, and alone entitled to Paradise.
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r2.anchor: Most commentators see this as a reference to spiritual assertions the Jews or the People of the Book are said to make elsewhere in the Quran

STUDYQURAN:4:49/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r3.speaker: a group of Madinan Jews
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r3.claim: Some say a group claimed to the Prophet that they were sinless, that daytime sins were forgiven at night, or that they could absolve one another through intercession; the Quran does not explicitly attest the claims.
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r3.anchor: Some say that it refers to a group of Madinan Jews who approached the Prophet, claiming that they were free of sin

STUDYQURAN:4:49/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r4.claim: The Quran warns everyone against considering themselves pure; God alone knows who is truly pure.
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r4.anchor: The Quran warns people in general not to consider themselves pure (53:32). God alone knows those who are truly pure and those who are not

STUDYQURAN:4:49/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r5.claim: Fatīl may be the date-stone thread or soil scraped between fingers, Quranic images of insignificance; here it means no one is wronged even slightly.
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r5.anchor: The thread of a date stone renders fatīl, which might also mean the bit of soil that one can find by scraping between one’s fingers

STUDYQURAN:4:49/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r7.claim: Joseph models refusal to claim purity: exposed treachery leads him to say he does not absolve his own soul, which commands evil.
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r7.anchor: Even the falsely accused prophet Joseph asserted, when the treachery of his would-be seductress was revealed, But I absolve not my own soul

STUDYQURAN:4:49/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r8.speaker: Sufis
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r8.claim: Sufis warn that the carnal soul is not the locus of human purity.
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r8.anchor: particularly odious to the Sufis, who warned that the carnal soul

STUDYQURAN:4:49/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r9.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r9.claim: Being pleased with one’s own soul extinguishes the lights of certitude.
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r9.anchor: being pleased with one’s own soul extinguished the lights of certitude (Su)

STUDYQURAN:4:49/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r10.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r10.claim: Self-satisfaction is a source of disobedience and heedlessness.
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r10.anchor: was the source of disobedience and heedlessness (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:4:49/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r11.speaker: Qu
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r11.claim: Anyone persuaded by praise of their purity or by their own self-estimation is veiled in ignorance.
STUDYQURAN:4:49/r11.anchor: anyone who was persuaded by others’ high opinions of their purity or by their own high estimation of themselves was veiled in ignorance (Qu)

TAB-FULL:v7p124/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r1.claim: The address asks Muḥammad to perceive in his heart those Jews who exonerate and purify themselves of sins.
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r1.anchor: فقال بعضهم: كانت تزكيتهم أنفسهم قولهم

TAB-FULL:v7p124/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r2.claim: Qatāda says the Jews claimed they were God’s children and beloved, and that they had no sins.
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم بل الله يزكي من يشاء ولا يظلمون فتيلا} [النساء: 49] وهم أعداء الله اليهود

TAB-FULL:v7p124/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies Jews and Christians, who claimed to be God’s children and beloved and said only Jews or Christians enter paradise.
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم} [النساء: 49] قال: " هم اليهود والنصارى، قالوا: {نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه}

TAB-FULL:v7p124/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Jews claimed to have no sins beyond those of their newborn children, reasoning that they were like them.
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك، قال: قالت يهود: ليست لنا ذنوب إلا كذنوب أولادنا يوم يولدون، فإن كانت لهم ذنوب

TAB-FULL:v7p124/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the People of the Book claimed paradise, God’s love, and obedience for themselves, including that only Jews or Christians enter paradise.
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم} [النساء: 49] قال: " قال أهل الكتاب: {لن يدخل الجنة إلا من كان هودا أو نصارى}

TAB-FULL:v7p124/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says Jews claimed their children learned Torah young and had no sins, and their own daytime sins were expiated at night.
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r6.anchor: عن السدي: {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم بل الله يزكي من يشاء ولا يظلمون فتيلا} [النساء: 49] نزلت في اليهود

TAB-FULL:v7p124/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r7.claim: Another reported explanation is that Jews appointed their children to lead prayer, claiming the children were sinless.
TAB-FULL:v7p124/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل كانت تزكيتهم أنفسهم تقديمهم أطفالهم لإمامتهم في صلاتهم زعما منها أنهم لا ذنوب لهم

TAB-FULL:v7p126/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r1.claim: Mujāhid says Jews appointed children to lead prayer because they claimed the children had no sins; this was their self-purification.
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {يزكون أنفسهم} [النساء: 49] قال: «يهود، كانوا يقدمون صبيانهم في الصلاة فيؤمونهم

TAB-FULL:v7p126/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r2.claim: Mujāhid further describes children leading supplication and prayer, with Ibn Jurayj identifying the group as Jews and Christians.
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: " كانوا يقدمون الصبيان أمامهم في الدعاء والصلاة يؤمونهم

TAB-FULL:v7p126/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r3.claim: Abū Mālik says the verse was revealed about Jews who put children forward, saying that they had no sins.
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r3.anchor: عن أبي مالك، في قوله: {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم} [النساء: 49] قال: " نزلت في اليهود

TAB-FULL:v7p126/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says the People of the Book put prepubescent boys forward to lead prayer, claiming they were sinless, and the verse was revealed in response.
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم}

TAB-FULL:v7p126/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Jews claimed their deceased children would be close to God and intercede to purify them.
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم} [النساء: 49] وذلك أن اليهود قالوا: إن أبناءنا قد توفوا

TAB-FULL:v7p126/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r6.claim: Another group interprets the phrase as some of the People of the Book declaring one another purified.
TAB-FULL:v7p126/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل ذلك كان منهم تزكية من بعضهم لبعض

TAB-FULL:v7p128/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the Jews claim to be free of sins and faults and to be God's sons and beloved; their self-purification is a false claim, as 4:50 confirms.
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r1.anchor: معنى تزكية القوم الذين وصفهم الله بأنهم يزكون أنفسهم ووصفهم إياها بأنها لا ذنوب لها ولا خطايا

TAB-FULL:v7p128/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r2.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r2.claim: Abdullah describes a man who flatters someone powerless to benefit or harm him in hope of securing a need, thereby angering God, and then recites this verse.
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله: إن الرجل ليغدو بدينه، ثم يرجع وما معه منه شيء.

TAB-FULL:v7p128/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r3.speaker: الذين قالوا
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r3.claim: Some interpreted the Jews' self-purification as presenting their children for prayer; al-Ṭabarī rejects this as unproved without an authoritative report establishing it.
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r3.anchor: وأما الذين قالوا: معنى ذلك: تقديمهم أطفالهم للصلاة، فتأويل لا تدرك صحته إلا بخبر حجة يوجب العلم

TAB-FULL:v7p128/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r4.claim: God alone purifies whom He wills, cleansing them from sin by enabling them to leave disobedience and obey Him; self-praise cannot make someone purified.
TAB-FULL:v7p128/r4.anchor: والله يزكي من يشاء من خلقه، فيطهره ويبرئه من الذنوب بتوفيقه لاجتناب ما يكرهه

TAB-FULL:v7p129/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r1.claim: God wrongs neither the self-purifying people nor anyone else by withholding or assigning purification, depriving anyone of a right, or placing anything out of its proper place.
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r1.anchor: غير ظالم أحدا ممن زكاه أو لم يزكه فتيلا

TAB-FULL:v7p129/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r2.claim: God gives success to whom He wills and leaves in failure whom He wills among the disobedient; this is God's choice, yet no one is wronged.
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r2.anchor: لكنه يزكي من يشاء من خلقه، فيوفقه، ويخذل من يشاء من أهل معاصيه؛ كل ذلك إليه

TAB-FULL:v7p129/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو العالية، أبو مالك، السدي
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r3.claim: Reports attributed to Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aliya, Abu Malik, and al-Suddi explain fatil as the grime that comes out when fingers or hands are rubbed together.
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: الفتيل: ما خرج من بين أصبعيك

TAB-FULL:v7p129/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains fatil as the material inside a date pit.
TAB-FULL:v7p129/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فتيلا} [النساء: 49] قال: «الذي في بطن النواة»

TAB-FULL:v7p133/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r1.speaker: عطاء، ابن زيد، عطية
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r1.claim: These authorities identify fatil with the material in the kernel of a date pit.
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r1.anchor: عن طلحة بن عمرو، عن عطاء، قال: الفتيل: الذي في بطن النواة

TAB-FULL:v7p133/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r2.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r2.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Dahhak locate fatil in the cleft of the kernel; other reports from Mujahid describe it as being in the seed.
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r2.anchor: أخبرني عبد الله بن كثير، أنه سمع مجاهدا، يقول: الفتيل: الذي في شق النواة

TAB-FULL:v7p133/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r3.claim: Fatil is morphologically derived from maftul, shifting from the passive participle pattern to faʿil, as sariʿ and dahin derive from masruʿ and madhun.
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r3.anchor: وأصل الفتيل: المفتول، صرف من مفعول إلى فعيل، كما قيل: صريع ودهين

TAB-FULL:v7p133/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r4.claim: Because the verse denies injustice even in the smallest things, all these insignificant twisted traces, whether finger grime or material in a kernel, fall within fatil unless evidence excludes one.
TAB-FULL:v7p133/r4.anchor: فواجب أن يكون كل ذلك داخلا في معنى الفتيل، إلا أن يخرج شيئا من ذلك

SULAMI:v1p149#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p149#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p149#3/r1.claim: The self is not a proper site for purification; admiring anything in oneself extinguishes the lights of certainty within.
SULAMI:v1p149#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : ليست الأنفس محل التزكية ، فمن استحسن من نفسه شيئا فقد اسقط عن باطنه أنوار اليقين

TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r2.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r2.claim: Al-Raghib derives zakat from growth produced by God’s blessing.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r2.anchor: قال الراغب أصل الزكاة النمو الحاصل من بركة الله تعالى

TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r3.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes commendable self-purification by deeds from blameworthy verbal self-praise, which God forbids as ethically ugly.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r3.anchor: وتزكية الإنسان نفسه ضربان أحدهما بالفعل وهو محمود

TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r4.claim: In this passage’s context, those praising themselves are Jews or some of them; persistence in this vice shows they have stripped themselves of scripture’s knowledge.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r4.anchor: كان الظاهر أن هؤلاء المزكين لأنفسهم هم أهل الكتاب أو بعضهم

TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r5.claim: Their claims to be God’s children and beloved, to face the Fire for only a few days, and to be His chosen friends illustrate the self-praise at issue.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#8/r5.anchor: ويؤيده ما حكاه الله تعالى عن اليهود من قولهم نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r1.claim: The verse alludes to Jews and supports the preceding account of their arrogance toward truth, refusal to believe, and divine curse as consequences of self-admiration.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r1.anchor: الآية تكني عن اليهود وفيها استشهاد لما تقدم ذكره في الآيات السابقة

TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r2.claim: The correction makes purification God’s prerogative: a person cannot treat any virtue as independently owned or rely on it as self-sufficient before God.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r2.anchor: إضراب عن تزكيتهم لأنفسهم ورد لهم فيما زكوه وبيان أن ذلك من شؤون الربوبية

TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r3.claim: Self-admiration is a root vice that grows into arrogance and then oppression, exploitation, and violations of people’s lives, honor, and property.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r3.anchor: وهذا الغرور والإعجاب الذي يبعث الإنسان إلى تزكية نفسه هو العجب الذي هو من أمهات الرذائل

TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r4.claim: When self-exalting pride becomes a social custom, as he says it did among Jews, it endangers humanity and corrupts the earth.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r4.anchor: وأما إذا تعدى الفرد وصار خلقا اجتماعيا وسيرة قومية فهو الخطر الذي فيه هلاك النوع وفساد الأرض

TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r5.claim: Only God may rightly praise or confer virtue because He owns what people possess; human self-praise claims an independence no creature has.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#9/r5.anchor: فما كان لبشر أن يذكر لنفسه من الفضيلة ما يمدحها به سواء كان صادقا فيما يقول أو كاذبا

TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r1.claim: God’s own spoken praise of prophets exemplifies legitimate verbal purification; al-Tabatabai cites Adam, Noah, Abraham, Idris, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Jesus, Solomon, Job, and Muhammad.

TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r2.claim: God’s purification is true and just, whether practical by bestowing favor or verbal by declaring someone praiseworthy; in this context it means verbal praise.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r2.anchor: أن تزكيته تعالى وإن كانت مطلقة تشمل التزكية العملية والتزكية القولية لكنها تنطبق بحسب مورد الكلام على التزكية القولية

TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r3.claim: One reported explanation of fitil is the fiber in the cleft of a date stone.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r3.anchor: قيل المراد به ما يكون في شق النواة

TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r4.claim: Another reported explanation is the material inside the date stone.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r4.anchor: وقيل هو ما في بطن النواة

TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r5.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r5.claim: Reports from the Imams of the Prophet’s Household identify fitil as the dot on a date stone, naqir as its back, and qitmir as its peel; no grading is stated.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r5.anchor: ورد في روايات عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أنه النقطة التي على النواة

TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r6.claim: A further reported meaning is dirt rolled between one’s fingers.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r6.anchor: وقيل هو ما فتلته بين إصبعيك من الوسخ

TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r7.claim: People should not praise themselves; others may praise a person only for virtues God recognizes, since religion determines which qualities count as virtues.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#10/r7.anchor: ليس لصاحب الفضل أن يعجبه فضله ويمدح نفسه بل هو مما يختص به تعالى

TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r1.claim: This teaching does not prohibit recognizing real virtue: people should honor scholars and defer to knowledge as following truth, though scholars must not boast of learning.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r1.anchor: فعلى الجاهل أن يخضع للعالم ويعرف له قدره فإنه من اتباع الحق

TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r2.speaker: بعض باحثينا
TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r2.claim: Some of the author’s fellow researchers, following Maghrebi thinkers, count reliance on oneself among human virtues.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r2.anchor: ما ذكره بعض باحثينا واتبعوا في ذلك ما ذكره المغاربة أن من الفضائل الإنسانية الاعتماد بالنفس

TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r3.claim: He rejects self-reliance as a virtue and says the Quran instead teaches reliance on God and deriving strength and honor from Him.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#11/r3.anchor: والذي يراه القرآن في ذلك هو الاعتماد بالله والتعزز بالله

TABRISI:4:49-50/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:49-50/r1.claim: Tazkiya means purification or declaring someone pure; its root zakā denotes growth, as when crops grow soundly.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r1.anchor: التزكية: التطهير والتنزيه وقد يكون الوصف بالتطهير تزكية وأصله من الزكاء

TABRISI:4:49-50/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:49-50/r2.claim: Fatīl comes from twisting; fatīla names the twisted strand, and a fatlāʾ she-camel has a twisted-looking forearm.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r2.anchor: وأصل الفتيل: ما يفتل وهو لي الشيء، والفتيلة معروفة وناقة فتلاء

TABRISI:4:49-50/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r3.speaker: النابغة
TABRISI:4:49-50/r3.claim: Fatīl can mean a trifling amount; al-Nābigha’s verse uses it for what an enemy loses of no account.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r3.anchor: قال النابغة: يجمع الجيش ذا الألوف ويغزو ثم لا يرزأ العدو فتيلا

TABRISI:4:49-50/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:49-50/r4.claim: Naẓar is turning one’s gaze toward something, or turning the heart toward it; it also describes looking with mercy, contemplation, expectation, disputation, and likeness.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r4.anchor: والنظر هو الإقبال على الشيء بالبصر، ومنه النظر بالقلب لأنه إقبال على الشيء بالقلب

TABRISI:4:49-50/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:49-50/r5.claim: Ruʾya is apprehending the object, whereas naẓar is directing sight toward it, so one may look without seeing; God may be called seeing but not looking.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r5.anchor: والفرق بين النظر والرؤية أن الرؤية هي إدراك المرئي، والنظر الإقبال بالبصر نحو المرئي

TABRISI:4:49-50/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r6.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:4:49-50/r6.claim: Ali ibn ʿIsa parses fatīlan as a second object, or alternatively as an accusative of specification.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r6.anchor: فتيلا منصوب على أنه مفعول ثان كقولك ظلمته حقه قال علي بن عيسى

TABRISI:4:49-50/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r7.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:4:49-50/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Jews who brought their children to the Prophet, asked whether they had sins, then claimed the same innocence for themselves; God refuted them.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r7.anchor: بالليل كفر عنا بالنهار فكذبهم الله، عن الكلبي.

TABRISI:4:49-50/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r8.speaker: الضحاك والحسن وقتادة والسدي وأبو جعفر
TABRISI:4:49-50/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Suddi, in a report also transmitted from al-Baqir, say it was revealed about Jews and Christians claiming to be God’s children and beloved and that only their groups enter Paradise.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك والحسن وقتادة والسدي وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر ع.

TABRISI:4:49-50/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:49-50/r9.claim: After discussing their unbelief and distortion of scripture, the passage turns to their self-purification claims.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r9.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى تزكية هؤلاء أنفسهم مع كفرهم وتحريفهم الكتاب فقال

TABRISI:4:49-50/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:49-50/r10.claim: Alam tara means “do you not know” or “have you not been told”; the question informs the Prophet and means, “Know their story.”
TABRISI:4:49-50/r10.anchor: { ألم تر } معناه ألم تعلم. وقيل: ألم تخبر. وهو سؤال على وجه الإعلام

TABRISI:4:49-50/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:49-50/r11.claim: They praise themselves and describe themselves as pure by saying, “We are pure.”
TABRISI:4:49-50/r11.anchor: أي يمدحونها ويصفونها بالزكاة والطهارة بأن يقولوا نحن أزكياء

TABRISI:4:49-50/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABRISI:4:49-50/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿud explains the phrase as their praising one another.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r12.anchor: وقيل: هو تزكية بعضهم بعضا عن ابن مسعود

TABRISI:4:49-50/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:49-50/r13.claim: The plural “themselves” fits because they share one religion and are like a single self.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r13.anchor: وإنما قال: أنفسهم لأنهم على دين واحد وهم كنفس واحدة

TABRISI:4:49-50/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:49-50/r14.claim: The correction means that God alone purifies whoever He wills, cleansing that person of sin.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r14.anchor: أي يطهر من الذنب من يشاء

TABRISI:4:49-50/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r15.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:4:49-50/r15.claim: An alternative says God accepts a person’s deeds and thereby makes that person pure; He does not purify the Jews but punishes them.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r15.anchor: وقيل: معناه يقبل عمله فيصير زكيا ولا يزكي اليهود بل يعذبهم.

TABRISI:4:49-50/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:49-50/r16.claim: They are not wronged by even a thread’s worth in being punished and denied purification.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r16.anchor: معناه لا يظلمون في تعذيبهم، وترك تزكيتهم فتيلا

TABRISI:4:49-50/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r17.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء وقتادة
TABRISI:4:49-50/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, ʿAtaʾ, and Qatada say fatīl is the groove in a date stone.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r17.anchor: فقيل: هو ما يكون في شق النواة عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطا وقتادة

TABRISI:4:49-50/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r18.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:4:49-50/r18.claim: Al-Hasan distinguishes fatīl inside the date stone, naqīr on its back, and qitmīr as its skin.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r18.anchor: وقيل: الفتيل ما في بطن النواة، والنقير ما على ظهرها والقطمير قشرها عن الحسن

TABRISI:4:49-50/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r19.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو مالك والسدي
TABRISI:4:49-50/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Abu Malik, and al-Suddi say fatīl is the dirt rubbed between two fingers.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r19.anchor: الفتيل ما فتلته بين إصبعيك من الوسخ عن ابن عباس وأبي مالك والسدي

TABRISI:4:49-50/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:49-50/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:49-50/r20.claim: The verse establishes God’s freedom from injustice: He wrongs no one, by even a little or a lot.
TABRISI:4:49-50/r20.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على تنزيه الله عن الظلم وإنما ذكر الفتيل ليعلم أنه لا يظلم قليلا ولا كثيرا

FARRA:v1p272/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p272/r5.speaker: اليهود
FARRA:v1p272/r5.claim: The Jews brought their children to the Prophet and claimed they were sinless, then said their nighttime deeds were erased by day and daytime deeds by night.
FARRA:v1p272/r5.anchor: جاءت اليهود بأولادها إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا : هل لهؤلاء

FARRA:v1p272/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p272/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p272/r6.claim: That claim is what the verse calls purifying themselves.
FARRA:v1p272/r6.anchor: ما عملناه بالليل كفر عنا بالنهار، وما عملناه بالنهار كفر عنا بالليل. فذلك تزكيتهم أنفسهم

FARRA:v1p272/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p272/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p272/r7.claim: Fatil can mean the dirt rolled between one’s fingers.
FARRA:v1p272/r7.anchor: ولا يظلمون فتيلا الفتيل هو ما فتلت بين إصبعيك من الوسخ،

FARRA:v1p272/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p272/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p272/r8.claim: Another explanation takes fatil as the filament inside a date stone.
FARRA:v1p272/r8.anchor: ويقال: هو الذي في بطن النواة.

THALABI:v3p326/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p326/r1.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
THALABI:v3p326/r1.claim: Mujahid and Ikrima say the Jews' self-purification was putting children forward in prayer on the claim that they had no sins.
THALABI:v3p326/r1.anchor: مجاهد وعكرمة: هو أنهم كانوا يقدمون أطفالهم في الصلاة يزعمون أنهم لا ذنب لهم،

THALABI:v3p326/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p326/r2.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p326/r2.claim: According to Ibn Abbas through Atiyya, Jews claimed deceased ancestors and children would intercede for them and purify them.
THALABI:v3p326/r2.anchor: عطية عن ابن عباس: هو أن اليهود قالوا: إن آباءنا وأبناءنا توفوا، فهم سيشفعون لنا

THALABI:v3p326/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p326/r3.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v3p326/r3.claim: Abdullah interprets the self-praise as people vouching for one another.
THALABI:v3p326/r3.anchor: وقال عبد الله: هو تزكية بعضهم لبعض،

THALABI:v3p326/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p326/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v3p326/r4.claim: Ibn Masud warns that flattery can strip a person of religion: one leaves home with faith, praises someone powerless to help or harm, and returns with none; he recited this verse.
THALABI:v3p326/r4.anchor: وعن طارق ابن شهاب قال: سمعت ابن مسعود يقول: إن الرجل ليغدو من بيته ومعه دينه،

THALABI:v3p326/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p326/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p326/r5.claim: God purifies from sins whomever He wills.
THALABI:v3p326/r5.anchor: بل الله يزكي أي يطهر من الذنوب من يشاء

THALABI:v3p326/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p326/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p326/r6.claim: A فتيل is either the strand in a date stone's cleft or dirt rubbed between the fingers; in the latter account it follows the فعيل pattern with passive meaning.
THALABI:v3p326/r6.anchor: وهو ما يكون في شق النواة، وقيل: هو ما فتلته بين إصبعيك من الوسخ فيكون فعيلا

THALABI:v3p326/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p326/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p326/r7.claim: An unnamed poet uses فتيل for a negligible amount, saying an army can campaign without the enemy suffering a thread's worth of loss.
THALABI:v3p326/r7.anchor: يجمع الجيش ذا الألوف فيغزو … ثم لا يرزأ العدو فتيلا

THALABI:v3p326/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p326/r9.speaker: السلمي
THALABI:v3p326/r9.claim: Al-Sulami reads ألم تره throughout the Quran; this dialect adds sukūn to the preceding consonant after deleting the jussive letter.
THALABI:v3p326/r9.anchor: قرأ السلمي: (ألم تره) في كل القرآن، وهي لغة قوم لا يكتفون من الجزم بحذف الحرف

THALABI:v3p326/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p326/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p326/r10.claim: The author illustrates the dialect's added sukūn with an anonymous line about whoever God guides or misguides.
THALABI:v3p326/r10.anchor: كقول الشاعر: من يهده الله يهتد لا مضل له … ومن أضل فما يهديه من هادي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r3.claim: Those praising their own purity are Jews who claimed to be God’s children and beloved, and that their sins were erased by the opposite part of each day.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r3.anchor: أي: اليهود قالوا: نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r4.claim: God makes whomever He wills pure and increases that person in righteousness; here this refers to monotheists.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r4.anchor: أي: يجعل من يشاء زاكيا طاهرا ناميا في الصلاح

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r5.claim: They are not deprived of even a thread-thin amount of reward; fatīl is the thin membrane around a date pit.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r5.anchor: لا ينقصون من الثواب قدر الفتيل، وهو القشرة الرقيقة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r6.claim: The author transitions to the following verse by saying that the Prophet is made to marvel at their lies.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:48-49/r6.anchor: ثم عجب نبيه عليه السلام من كذبهم، فقال:

ELMALILI:4:49-50/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r1.claim: A report says Jewish leaders Huyay ibn Akhtab and Ka'b ibn Ashraf traveled to Mecca with seventy Jewish horsemen to make an alliance with Quraysh and break their pact with the Prophet.
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r1.anchor: Huyey b. Ahtab ile Ka‘b b. Eşref ma‘iyyetlerine Yehûddan yetmiş süvari alarak Mekke’ye gitmişler ve Kureyş ile bir ittifak ve mu‘âhede akdederek Resûlullah ile olan ahidlerini nakz etmek istemişlerdi

ELMALILI:4:49-50/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r2.claim: Quraysh asked the Jews to prostrate to their idols as proof of trust, saying they could not rely on them because they were People of Scripture and closer to Muhammad.
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r2.anchor: siz ehl-i kitabsınız, Muhammed’e bizden daha yakınsınız. Binâen‘aleyh biz size emin olamayız, bizim mâbudlarımıza secde ediniz de mutmain olalım

ELMALILI:4:49-50/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r3.claim: The Jewish leaders immediately accepted Quraysh's demand to prostrate to the idols.
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r3.anchor: Yahudîler de derhâl kabul edip yapıvermişler

ELMALILI:4:49-50/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r4.claim: Abu Sufyan asked Ka'b which path was right; after hearing that Muhammad called only to worship God and reject idolatry, Ka'b praised Quraysh's own religious services and judged their path better.
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r4.anchor: sen kitab okur âlim bir adamsın, biz ise ümmîyiz bilmeyiz.

ELMALILI:4:49-50/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r5.claim: Ka'b preferred the polytheists over the believers; Elmalılı identifies this episode as the subject of these verses.
ELMALILI:4:49-50/r5.anchor: putperestleri ehl-i imana tafdil ve tercih etmiş idi ki şu âyetler bunun hakkındadır

MAJAZ:v1p129/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p129/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p129/r2.claim: ‘Have you not seen?’ is not literal eyesight here; it calls attention in the sense ‘Have you not known?’
MAJAZ:v1p129/r2.anchor: ألم تر إلى الذين» (49) ليس هذا رأى عين، هذا تنبيه فى معنى: ألم تعرف.

MAJAZ:v1p129/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p129/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p129/r3.claim: Fatīl is the thread in the groove of a date stone.
MAJAZ:v1p129/r3.anchor: فتيلا» (49) ، الفتيل الذي فى شق النواة.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r1.claim: Tazkiya can be done by action or speech; improving character and undergoing moral education to escape bad traits are approved and encouraged.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r1.anchor: şeklinde tercüme edilen tezkiye fiil ve sözle olmaktadır. İnsanın ahlâkını iyileştirmek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r2.claim: Verbal tazkiya means saying someone is honest, good, or free of major faults; praising someone known to be so can be appropriate or necessary depending on circumstances.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r2.anchor: suretiyle yapılır. Gerçekten böyle olan, böyle bilinen birisi için gerektiğinde tezkiyede bulunmak da sakıncalı değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r3.claim: What Islam condemns and forbids is a person verbally purifying and praising themself.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r3.anchor: İslâm’da kötü görülen, menedilen tezkiye, kişinin kendisini sözle tezkiye etmesidir, övmesidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r4.claim: The verse condemns Jews' verbal self-praise as God's children and beloved, His friends, and people who will suffer punishment only a few days; such praise cannot confer status or esteem.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:49/r4.anchor: söyleyerek kendileri için sözlü tezkiyede bulunmuşlardı; âyet bu davranışı da mahkûm etmekte, kişilerin veya grupların kendilerini överek bir yere varamayacaklarını

NAHHAS:v1p461/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p461/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p461/r9.claim: The self-purifying people call themselves obedient and allies; the Prophet is astonished at that claim.
NAHHAS:v1p461/r9.anchor: أي يسميه مطيعا ووليا ثم عجب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من ذلك

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p70/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p70/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، مجاهد، أبو مالك
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p70/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Jews put their boys forward to lead prayer and offer sacrifices, claiming they had no sins; similar reports are attributed to ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, Abū Mālik, and others.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p70/r2.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس قال كانت اليهود يقدمون صبيانهم يصلون بهم ويقربون قربانهم يزعمون أنهم لا خطايا لهم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p155/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p155/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p155/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says Jews came to Muhammad with their children and asked whether the children bore sin; when he said no, they claimed they too were like them, with each day’s sins erased by night and each night’s by day. This was their self-purification.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p155/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: نزلت في رجال من اليهود أتوا رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بأطفالهم وقالوا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r15.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r15.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r15.claim: Fatīl is the fiber in a date pit's cleft and naqīr its back dimple; neither is meant literally, but both express that judgment will wrong no one even by a negligible amount.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r15.anchor: والفتيل: ما يكون في شق النواة. والنقير: النقرة في ظهرها. ولم يرد أنهم لا يظلمون ذلك بعينه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r1.claim: Several cited lexicons define fatil as the thread-like line in a date pit's groove; some also cite another poem for the term.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r1.anchor: واقتصر في (تق، ك، ط) على: التي تكون في شق النواة وشاهده في الثلاثة قول النابغة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r2.speaker: النابغة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r2.claim: Al-Nabigha's line uses fatil for an extremely tiny amount, saying enemies are not deprived even of it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r2.anchor: يجمع الجيش ذا الألوف ويغزو. . . ثم لا يرزأ الأعادى فتيلا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r3.speaker: الفراء وابن قتيبة والطبري والقرطبي والراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r3.claim: Authorities also explain fatil as what one twists between the fingers, such as thread or dirt; figuratively it denotes the smallest, most insignificant thing, which God does not wrong anyone by.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r3.anchor: ما تفتله بين أصابعك من خيط أو وسخ

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r4.claim: All three Qur'anic occurrences concern God's reckoning of people and assert that no one is wronged even by the tiniest amount.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p476/r4.anchor: وليس في القرآن من المادة سواها. وسياقها جميعاً في حساب الله تعالى عباده، لا يظلم أحدٌ فتيلاً
